input.strategy_title: Default Vector Store for Gen AI Studio and Auto Rag
input.strategy_markdown:
## Summary

RHOAI must provide a default vector store that is available out-of-the-box — without manual setup — so that Gen AI Studio and Auto Rag continue to function when inline providers are removed from the Llama Stack distribution image. Today these capabilities depend on an inline vector store provider bundled within the Llama Stack process; removing it (per RHAISTRAT-7474) will break them unless an alternative is available at the platform level.

## Problem Statement

Gen AI Studio and Auto Rag currently rely on an inline Milvus provider embedded in the Llama Stack distribution image to store and retrieve vector embeddings. This inline provider runs inside the Llama Stack process itself.

RHAISTRAT-7474 proposes removing inline providers from the Llama Stack distribution to improve GA readiness — shipping only what can be tested and maintained at scale, and aligning with Llama Stack's primary use case as a remote API server. However, no platform-level alternative exists today. If inline providers are removed without a replacement, any RHOAI user relying on Gen AI Studio's RAG capabilities or Auto Rag will lose functionality entirely — there is no workaround short of manually provisioning and configuring an external vector database.

Users expect vector storage to "just work" when they use Gen AI Studio or Auto Rag. The current out-of-the-box experience must be preserved even as the underlying architecture evolves.

## Affected Customers

* All RHOAI customers using Gen AI Studio playground with RAG capabilities
* All RHOAI customers using Auto Rag
* This is a platform-level product dependency: these features cannot function without a vector store

## Business Justification

* **Product integrity:** Gen AI Studio and Auto Rag are GA-track capabilities in RHOAI. Removing the inline vector store without a replacement breaks shipped product functionality for every user of these features.
* **Blocking dependency:** RHAISTRAT-7474 (removing inline providers for GA readiness) cannot proceed until this RFE is resolved. Silas Brenmark (Gen AI Studio lead) has identified this as a blocker.
* **User experience:** RHOAI differentiates on integrated, opinionated defaults. Requiring users to manually provision and configure a vector database before they can use the playground or Auto Rag degrades the out-of-the-box experience that customers expect from the platform.

## Acceptance Criteria

* \[ \] A default vector store is available out-of-the-box on RHOAI without requiring users to manually provision or configure external infrastructure
* \[ \] Gen AI Studio playground RAG workflows function with the default vector store with no loss of current capability
* \[ \] Auto Rag functions with the default vector store with no loss of current capability
* \[ \] The default vector store runs as a separate process, decoupled from the Llama Stack instance (not an inline provider)
* \[ \] The default vector store is scoped appropriately for multi-tenant environments (e.g., per-namespace isolation)
* \[ \] The default vector store is lightweight enough to run in resource-constrained environments without imposing significant overhead

## Success Criteria

* Users of Gen AI Studio and Auto Rag experience no functional regression when inline providers are removed from the Llama Stack distribution
* No additional manual setup steps are required for RAG workflows compared to the current experience
* RHAISTRAT-7474 is unblocked and can proceed to implementation

## Open Questions

* What is the preferred scoping model — per namespace, per Llama Stack instance, or both? (Silas noted per-namespace is preferred for isolation, but Auto Rag may need per-instance scoping)
* Should users have a migration path from the default vector store to a production-grade vector database? (Bram Sundqvist raised the importance of aligning with commonly-used vector DB providers for easier migration)

## Strategy (AI Generated by Agentic SDLC Pipeline)

> **Note:** The full strategy exceeds Jira's description size limit and is stored as an attachment: `RHAISTRAT-8004-strategy.md`.

## Staff Engineer Input

**Correction 1 — OGX does not auto-provision PostgreSQL.** OGX defaults to SQLite for storage (`storage.kv.type: sqlite`, `storage.sql.type: sqlite` in the OGXServer CRD). The odh-dashboard gen-ai BFF hardcodes SQLite when creating OGXServer instances for the playground (`kv_sqlite` and `sql_sqlite` in `llamastack_config.go`). PostgreSQL is a supported backend but must be user-configured with an explicit `connectionString` secret. The strategy's claim that "every LlamaStackDistribution instance requires a PostgreSQL database" is incorrect — introducing PostgreSQL is new work, not an extension of existing infrastructure.

**Correction 2 — A Red Hat PostgreSQL image with pgvector already exists.** The `registry.redhat.io/rhel9/postgresql-16` image includes pgvector out of the box — confirmed in the [sclorg/postgresql-container Dockerfile](https://github.com/sclorg/postgresql-container/blob/master/16/Dockerfile.rhel9) (`INSTALL_PKGS="$INSTALL_PKGS pgvector"`). PostgreSQL 18 (RHEL 9) also includes pgvector. Furthermore, the model-registry-operator already uses `postgresql-16` as its auto-provisioned database image, and `RELATED_IMAGE_POSTGRESQL_16_IMAGE` is already present in the rhods-operator CSV for disconnected installs. No custom image build is needed. No Konflux onboarding is needed. The 1-2 sprint image onboarding estimate in the strategy can be eliminated.

**Architectural direction — platform-level database vs. self-provisioned.** Multiple RHOAI components now need PostgreSQL (model-registry, MLflow, and now OGX for pgvector). The preferred long-term direction is a platform-provided shared PostgreSQL managed via the DSC, where each component consumes a connection string rather than self-provisioning. A shared platform-provided PostgreSQL via DSC will not be available until RHOAI 3.6. For 3.5, Gen AI Studio must provision its own PostgreSQL instance.

**Operator dependency for self-provisioning (RHAISTRAT-7164).** Self-provisioning PostgreSQL following the model-registry-operator pattern requires a RHOAI-controlled operator for Gen AI Studio. The ogx-k8s-operator is upstream and cannot carry RHOAI-specific provisioning logic. The dashboard operator modularization (RHAISTRAT-7164, In Progress) would provide this operator layer. This is a hard dependency — until RHAISTRAT-7164 delivers, there is no RHOAI-controlled operator where PostgreSQL lifecycle management can live. It will be challenging to commit this strategy to a specific release until that dependency is delivered.

**Fallback if RHAISTRAT-7164 does not land in time.** If the dashboard modularization is not ready for 3.5, the fallback is to require customers to bring their own PostgreSQL for RAG capabilities in the Playground. Users would manually configure the OGXServer CR spec with their PostgreSQL connection details. This aligns with the breaking changes introduced in OGX 1.0, even though the Playground largely abstracts OGX from users. The development team should define a go/no-go gate for this decision as part of sprint planning.

**Decouple from Auto Rag.** Auto Rag integration with Gen AI Studio (RHAISTRAT-7824) is targeting RHOAI 3.6. This strategy should validate pgvector only for Gen AI Studio Playground RAG workflows. Auto Rag compatibility with pgvector will be addressed in RHAISTRAT-7824's scope. Remove Auto Rag from affected components, impacted teams, acceptance criteria, and validation requirements.

**Performance and index thresholds — dev experimentation scope.** The default pgvector instance is meant for development experimentation, not production usage. Strict latency SLAs (p50/p95/p99) are not required. The sprint 1 benchmark should capture the inline Milvus baseline and verify pgvector is in the same order of magnitude, not meet a specific threshold. Typical Playground RAG usage involves small document sets — flat scan (no index) is sufficient for the default. Users with production-scale vector workloads should use an external vector database. Remove open questions about latency thresholds, corpus size ranges, and index type selection.

**PostgreSQL resource sizing.** Reference the model-registry-operator's PostgreSQL resource requests/limits as the starting point. Adjust based on sprint 1 benchmarking if needed.

**Alternative fallback — BFF-managed PostgreSQL provisioning.** If RHAISTRAT-7164 does not land in time, an alternative to requiring customers to bring their own PostgreSQL is to have the gen-ai BFF provision the PostgreSQL/pgvector instance directly, similar to how the BFF currently provisions guardrails infrastructure. The BFF would create the PostgreSQL Deployment, Service, PVC, and Secret when a playground with RAG is configured, if one does not already exist in the namespace. Caveats: (1) the implementation must be designed for portability — when the platform-provided shared database becomes available (3.6), the BFF should consume the shared connection string rather than self-provisioning; (2) lifecycle management of the PostgreSQL instance must be carefully considered — the BFF is not an operator with a reconciliation loop, so cleanup on playground deletion, handling of pod restarts, and credential rotation need explicit design attention.

**Existing remote vector store implementation is reusable.** Per the engineering team, the existing remote vector store implementation can be largely reused for pgvector integration. The majority of the work effort is around infrastructure and provisioning of the PostgreSQL/pgvector database, not the vector_io provider integration itself.

**Correction 3 — Vector storage and application storage are independent configurations.** The OGX vector_io provider configuration (`remote::pgvector` via `ENABLE_PGVECTOR`) is completely separate from OGX's application storage backend configuration (`storage.kv.type`, `storage.sql.type`). This strategy only needs to configure the pgvector vector_io provider — it does not change the application storage backend, which remains on its existing default (SQLite). There is no SQLite-to-PostgreSQL migration concern because the application storage is not being touched. Remove any references to consolidating vector and application storage in a single database, and remove any SQLite-to-PostgreSQL upgrade path considerations.

# Operator-based PostgreSQL self-provisioning for Gen AI Studio (operator path)

## Description

This branch epic applies when the provisioning-approach decision selects
operator-based self-provisioning — i.e. the RHOAI-controlled operator layer
delivered by the dashboard operator modularization will be available for
RHOAI 3.5. It implements PostgreSQL/pgvector self-provisioning for Gen AI
Studio playgrounds in that operator layer, following the model-registry-operator's
auto-provisioned database pattern, so that a default vector store works
out-of-the-box with no manual setup. The upstream ogx-k8s-operator cannot
carry this logic; it lives in the RHOAI-controlled operator layer.

## Scope

- In the RHOAI-controlled operator layer provided by the dashboard operator
  modularization: manage the lifecycle of an auto-provisioned PostgreSQL
  instance for Gen AI Studio playgrounds (Deployment, Service, credentials
  secret), following the model-registry-operator's auto-provisioning pattern.
- Use the existing Red Hat PostgreSQL 16 image, which already includes pgvector
  — no custom image build and no new build-pipeline onboarding; reuse the
  existing related-image reference so disconnected installs resolve the image.
- Scope the provisioned instance per namespace (per the scoping-model decision)
  for multi-tenant isolation.
- Ensure the provisioned instance's connection details flow into the
  playground's OGXServer remote pgvector vector_io provider configuration, so
  a playground with RAG works out of the box with zero manual steps.
- Design for portability: the component consumes a connection string rather
  than owning provisioning indefinitely — when the platform-provided shared
  PostgreSQL (managed via the DSC) becomes available in RHOAI 3.6, switching to
  the shared connection string is a configuration change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A user creates a playground with RAG enabled and a working default vector
  store exists with zero manual provisioning or configuration steps.
- The provisioned PostgreSQL runs as a separate process from the OGX instance,
  scoped per namespace (multi-tenant isolation), and the playground's vector
  traffic goes through the remote pgvector provider.
- Resource requests/limits for the provisioned instance are set from the
  agreed reference sizing (model-registry-operator values adjusted by the
  benchmark results).
- No custom container image is built or onboarded for this capability: the
  existing Red Hat PostgreSQL image with pgvector is used via the existing
  related-image reference.
- Switching the playground to a platform-provided shared PostgreSQL connection
  string requires configuration only (portability verified).
- Playground deletion cleans up the provisioned PostgreSQL resources the
  operator created for it.

## HLR Traceability

- AC-1 (default vector store available out-of-the-box without manual
  provisioning of external infrastructure).
- AC-2 (playground RAG workflows function with the default vector store, no
  loss of capability) — completes the out-of-box path on top of the provider
  configuration capability.
- AC-4 (separate process, decoupled from the OGX instance).
- AC-5 (multi-tenant scoping, per-namespace isolation).
- SE-2 (portability to the 3.6 platform-shared PostgreSQL via connection
  string).

## Risks / Notes

- Hard precondition: the dashboard operator modularization (RHAISTRAT-7164)
  must deliver the RHOAI-controlled operator layer; this epic exists only on
  that outcome. If the operator layer is not ready for 3.5, self-provisioning
  falls back to the BFF-managed path or to bring-your-own PostgreSQL.
- The upstream ogx-k8s-operator is not modified by this epic.

# BFF-managed PostgreSQL provisioning for Gen AI Studio (fallback path)

## Description

This branch epic applies when the provisioning-approach decision selects the
fallback in which the gen-ai BFF provisions the PostgreSQL/pgvector instance
directly — used when the RHOAI-controlled operator layer from the dashboard
operator modularization is not ready in time for RHOAI 3.5. When a playground
with RAG is configured and no suitable PostgreSQL instance exists in the
namespace, the BFF creates one, similar to how it already provisions guardrails
infrastructure. It builds on the pgvector provider configuration capability in
the same BFF surface, supplying the provisioned connection details to it.

## Scope

- The gen-ai BFF creates the PostgreSQL Deployment, Service, PVC, and Secret —
  using the existing Red Hat PostgreSQL 16 image, which already includes
  pgvector — when a playground with RAG is configured and no suitable instance
  exists in the namespace.
- Implement the lifecycle management the Staff Engineer Input flags as needing
  explicit design attention, since the BFF is not an operator with a
  reconciliation loop:
  - cleanup of provisioned resources on playground deletion (when no other
    playground in the namespace uses them);
  - idempotent handling of BFF pod restarts so instances are neither orphaned
    nor duplicated;
  - credential rotation for the provisioned instance.
- Design for portability: when the platform-provided shared PostgreSQL becomes
  available (RHOAI 3.6), the BFF consumes the shared connection string rather
  than self-provisioning.
- Wire the provisioned instance's connection details into the playground's
  OGXServer remote pgvector vector_io provider configuration, scoped per
  namespace for multi-tenant isolation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Configuring a playground with RAG in a fresh namespace results in a working
  default vector store with no manual provisioning or configuration steps by
  the user.
- The provisioned PostgreSQL runs as a separate process from the OGX instance,
  scoped per namespace, and the playground's vector traffic goes through the
  remote pgvector provider.
- Deleting a playground cleans up the PostgreSQL resources provisioned for it
  when no other playground in the namespace uses them.
- A restart of the BFF pod neither orphans nor duplicates the provisioned
  instance (idempotent reconciliation behavior verified by test).
- The credential rotation approach is implemented and verified.
- Switching the BFF to consume a platform-provided shared PostgreSQL
  connection string (3.6) requires configuration only (portability verified).
- Resource requests/limits for the provisioned instance follow the agreed
  reference sizing (model-registry-operator values adjusted by the benchmark
  results).

## HLR Traceability

- AC-1 (default vector store available out-of-the-box without manual
  provisioning of external infrastructure).
- AC-2 (playground RAG workflows function with the default vector store, no
  loss of capability) — completes the out-of-box path on top of the provider
  configuration capability.
- AC-4 (separate process, decoupled from the OGX instance).
- AC-5 (multi-tenant scoping, per-namespace isolation).
- SE-2 (portability to the 3.6 platform-shared PostgreSQL via connection
  string).

## Risks / Notes

- This path exists only if the provisioning-approach decision selects it as
  the fallback; if the operator layer lands in time, operator-based
  self-provisioning is preferred, and if BFF-managed provisioning is deemed
  too risky, the fallback is bring-your-own PostgreSQL only.
- The BFF is not an operator: lifecycle correctness (cleanup, restarts,
  credential rotation) is the principal design risk and is covered by explicit
  acceptance criteria above.

# Decide the default vector store provisioning approach for Gen AI Studio

## Description

This investigation resolves how the default pgvector-backed PostgreSQL instance
is provisioned for Gen AI Studio playground RAG in RHOAI 3.5, so that removing
the inline vector providers from the OGX distribution does not break playground
RAG. It produces the go/no-go decision the Staff Engineer Input requires the
development team to define as part of sprint planning: operator-based
self-provisioning (if the RHOAI-controlled operator layer from the dashboard
operator modularization, RHAISTRAT-7164, lands in time for 3.5), BFF-managed
provisioning by the gen-ai BFF, or bring-your-own PostgreSQL only. It also
fixes the scoping model for the default store (per namespace vs per OGX
instance).

## Scope

- Define explicit go/no-go criteria for operator-based provisioning in 3.5,
  tied to the delivery status of the dashboard operator modularization
  (RHAISTRAT-7164, In Progress), and drive the gate to an outcome.
- Compare the two self-provisioning options, both following the
  model-registry-operator's auto-provisioned PostgreSQL pattern:
  - Operator-based: PostgreSQL lifecycle management lives in the RHOAI-controlled
    operator layer (the ogx-k8s-operator is upstream and cannot carry
    RHOAI-specific provisioning logic).
  - BFF-managed: the gen-ai BFF creates the PostgreSQL Deployment, Service,
    PVC, and Secret when a playground with RAG is configured and no suitable
    instance exists in the namespace, similar to how the BFF already provisions
    guardrails infrastructure.
- If BFF-managed provisioning is a candidate, produce the explicit lifecycle
  design the Staff Engineer Input calls out: cleanup on playground deletion,
  handling of pod restarts (the BFF is not an operator with a reconciliation
  loop), and credential rotation.
- Evaluate portability requirements: whichever approach is chosen must be
  designed to consume a platform-provided shared PostgreSQL connection string
  when it becomes available in RHOAI 3.6, rather than self-provisioning
  forever.
- Decide the scoping model — per namespace (preferred for isolation) vs per
  OGX instance — noting that Auto Rag is out of scope for this strategy.
- Deliverable: a decision document recording the go/no-go outcome, the selected
  provisioning approach with rationale, the scoping model, and the enumerated
  downstream implementation scope for the selected approach.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The decision document records a go/no-go outcome for operator-based
  provisioning in 3.5, with explicit criteria tied to the dashboard operator
  modularization delivery status (not an open-ended "wait and see").
- The selected approach is exactly one of: operator-based self-provisioning,
  BFF-managed provisioning, or bring-your-own PostgreSQL only, with a rationale
  that compares lifecycle management, portability to the 3.6 platform-shared
  database, and release risk.
- If BFF-managed provisioning is selected or kept as the leading fallback, the
  decision document contains a lifecycle design covering cleanup on playground
  deletion, pod-restart handling, and credential rotation.
- The scoping model (per namespace or per instance) is decided with rationale.
- The downstream implementation scope for the selected approach is enumerated:
  which resources are created, which configuration surfaces change, and what
  the acceptance path is for the out-of-box default.

## HLR Traceability

- AC-5 (multi-tenant scoping, e.g. per-namespace isolation): the scoping model
  is decided here and implemented downstream.
- SE-2 (portability to the 3.6 platform-shared PostgreSQL): the portability
  constraint is evaluated and carried into the selected approach's design.
- Staff directive: define the go/no-go gate for the RHAISTRAT-7164 dependency
  as part of sprint planning.

## Risks / Notes

- Hard external dependency: RHAISTRAT-7164 (dashboard operator modularization)
  is In Progress with timing not controlled by this team; per the Staff
  Engineer Input, the strategy cannot be committed to a specific release until
  that dependency is delivered or the fallback is chosen. This epic is the
  gate that resolves that uncertainty.

# Configure the pgvector vector_io provider for Gen AI Studio playground

## Description

This epic makes Gen AI Studio playground RAG use OGX's existing remote pgvector
vector_io provider, backed by a PostgreSQL database, instead of depending on
the inline Milvus provider that is being removed from the OGX distribution.
The gen-ai BFF creates OGXServer instances for the playground; this epic
extends that configuration path so playgrounds with RAG get the remote pgvector
provider, including a bring-your-own path where the user supplies PostgreSQL
connection details. Per the Staff Engineer Input, the existing remote vector
store implementation is largely reusable — the work is configuration and
wiring, not a new provider.

## Scope

- When the gen-ai BFF creates or updates OGXServer instances for playgrounds
  with RAG enabled, set the remote pgvector vector_io provider configuration
  (activated via the distribution's pgvector provider environment guard) with
  PostgreSQL connection details sourced from a secret.
- Support a user-provided (bring-your-own) PostgreSQL connection string so
  playground RAG functions with no platform-provisioned database — this is the
  fallback path if platform self-provisioning is not available in 3.5, and it
  unblocks validation work independently of the provisioning decision.
- Leave OGX application storage configuration untouched: vector storage and
  application storage are independent configurations, and the application
  storage backend remains on its existing SQLite default. No storage
  consolidation and no SQLite-to-PostgreSQL migration is introduced.
- Verify, and capture as configuration guidance, that switching from the
  default pgvector store to an external vector database is a configuration
  change of the vector_io provider — this addresses the strategy's open
  question about a migration path to production-grade vector databases.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A playground with RAG enabled, configured with a user-provided PostgreSQL
  instance (with pgvector), stores and retrieves vector embeddings through the
  remote pgvector provider: document upload, embedding, retrieval, and
  generation complete successfully.
- The vector store in use runs as a separate process, decoupled from the OGX
  instance (a remote provider, not an inline provider bundled in the OGX
  process).
- OGX application storage configuration is unchanged from its existing default
  (no SQLite-to-PostgreSQL migration is introduced by this change).
- Switching the vector_io provider from the default pgvector store to an
  external vector database is achievable through configuration only, and the
  required configuration is captured as guidance.

## HLR Traceability

- AC-2 (playground RAG workflows function with the default vector store, no
  loss of current capability): this epic delivers the provider path; full
  no-loss verification is completed by the validation and benchmark work.
- AC-4 (default vector store runs as a separate process, not an inline
  provider): delivered by selecting the remote pgvector provider.
- SE-1 (bring-your-own PostgreSQL support via user-configured connection
  details).
- SE-4 (application storage untouched; no storage migration).

## Risks / Notes

- The ogx-distribution already ships the remote pgvector provider (inline
  providers are stripped from the distribution build); no OGX code change is
  expected. If the provider guard or its configuration surface turns out to
  require distribution changes, that scope must be re-evaluated against the
  OGX distribution component.

# Validate and benchmark pgvector as the default vector store for playground RAG

## Description

This epic validates that the remote pgvector provider preserves the current
Gen AI Studio playground RAG capability, and produces the dev-experimentation
benchmark and resource sizing that the Staff Engineer Input defines: capture
the inline Milvus baseline, verify pgvector is in the same order of magnitude
(not a specific latency threshold), and derive PostgreSQL resource sizing from
the model-registry-operator's reference values. It builds on the pgvector
provider configuration capability for the playground.

## Scope

- Capture the inline Milvus provider baseline for representative playground RAG
  workflows (document upload, embedding, retrieval, generation) before inline
  providers are removed from the OGX distribution.
- Benchmark the remote pgvector provider on the same workflows using a flat
  scan (no index), which is sufficient for typical playground document sets;
  verify the result is the same order of magnitude as the inline baseline. No
  latency SLAs (p50/p95/p99) and no corpus-size or index-type selection — the
  default store is for development experimentation, not production usage.
- Functionally validate playground RAG workflows end to end against pgvector
  with no loss of current capability, including the bring-your-own PostgreSQL
  path.
- Derive recommended PostgreSQL resource requests/limits for the default
  instance, starting from the model-registry-operator's PostgreSQL resource
  values as the reference point and adjusting based on the benchmark data;
  confirm the default instance is lightweight enough for resource-constrained
  environments.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The inline Milvus baseline for the representative workflows is captured and
  recorded (methodology, workloads, results).
- The benchmark report shows pgvector (flat scan) within the same order of
  magnitude as the inline baseline for the representative workflows.
- Each representative playground RAG workflow passes functionally against the
  remote pgvector provider with no loss of capability compared to the current
  inline-provider experience.
- Recommended PostgreSQL resource requests/limits are documented, derived from
  the model-registry-operator reference and the benchmark data, and are small
  enough for resource-constrained environments.

## HLR Traceability

- AC-2 (playground RAG workflows function with the default vector store, no
  loss of current capability): this epic is the measured verification.
- AC-6 (lightweight enough for resource-constrained environments without
  significant overhead): bundled here — it is measured by the same benchmark
  run and sizing analysis that verify AC-2; splitting it would duplicate the
  experiment.
- SE-3 (resource sizing referenced from the model-registry-operator, adjusted
  by benchmarking).

## Risks / Notes

- The benchmark can run against a manually or user-provisioned PostgreSQL
  instance; it does not depend on the outcome of the provisioning-approach
  decision.
- If pgvector is not within the same order of magnitude as the inline Milvus
  baseline for typical playground usage, the default-store choice must be
  re-evaluated before inline providers are removed.
